notes: First wife of Frederick Granger Williams (1787), Counselor in the First Presidency. After Frederick's death on October 10, 1842, she traveled to Utah in 1849 with her son Ezra Granger Williams (who founded the first hospital west of the Mississippi in Salt Lake City). On February 7, 1846, in the Nauvoo Temple, she was sealed for eternity to her husband Frederick G. Williams and married for time to Apostle Heber C. Kimball.

notes: Daughter of Swiss-French LDS convert Serge Louis Ballif and Elise Marie LeCoultre. Born in Switzerland, emigrated to Utah with family traveling in the 1854 Robert L. Campbell Company (listed as age 4). Married George Taft Benson Sr. (son of Apostle Ezra T. Benson 1811) on December 20, 1867 at the Endowment House in Salt Lake City; they had 13 children, including Serge Ballif Benson (b. 1877) named in honor of her father. Her sister Marie Jeanne Ballif married Aaron Dunham Thatcher (brother of Apostle Moses Thatcher), creating the genealogical bridge connecting the Benson cluster to the main cluster.

notes: Daughter of Swiss-French LDS convert Serge Louis Ballif and Elise Marie LeCoultre. Born in Switzerland; age 2 when traveling with the family in the 1854 Robert L. Campbell Company to Utah. Sister of Louisa Alexandrine Ballif (who married George Taft Benson Sr., son of Apostle Ezra T. Benson 1811). Married Aaron Dunham Thatcher (1837-1909) on April 10, 1871; Aaron was a brother of Apostle Moses Thatcher. This sibling-spouse chain bridges the Benson cluster (ETB 1811, ETB 1899) to the main cluster (Moses Thatcher).

notes: Brother of Apostle Moses Thatcher. Son of Hezekiah Thatcher (1808) and Alena Kitchen (1808). One of several Thatcher siblings who joined the LDS Church and settled in Cache Valley, Utah; his siblings include Joseph Wycoff, John Bethewel, George Washington, Moses, Hyrum Smith, and others. Married Marie Jeanne Ballif (sister of Louisa Ballif, wife of George Taft Benson Sr.) on April 10, 1871 in Logan, Utah. His children include Edgar Ballif Thatcher, Louise Ballif Thatcher, and Harriett Ballif Thatcher, honoring their Ballif maternal heritage. Died September 8, 1909 in Logan, Cache County, Utah.

notes: Daughter of Apostle Charles C. Rich's son Benjamin Erastus Rich (1855-1914) and his wife Diana Farr Rich (1858-1926). Ben E. notes: U.S. Senator from Utah (1947–1959), born February 1, 1886 in Midway, Wasatch County, Utah. Son of Arthur Watkins and Emily Adkins. Served as presiding judge of the Senate subcommittee that censured Senator Joseph McCarthy in 1954. Married Andrea Rich (daughter of Ben E. Rich, son of Apostle Charles C. Rich) on June 18, 1913. Their daughter Jeanene Watkins (born June 30, 1929) married Apostle Richard G. Scott on July 16, 1953 in the Manti Temple. Died September 1, 1973 in Orem, Utah.

notes: Daughter of U.S. Senator Arthur V. Watkins (1886-1973) and Andrea Rich Watkins (1890-1971). Andrea Rich was the daughter of Benjamin Erastus Rich (1855-1914), who was a son of Apostle Charles C. Rich (1809-1883). Born June 30, 1929 in Orem, Utah. Married Richard G.
